title: Tiramisu
subtitle: Classic Italian coffee and mascarpone dessert
excerpt: Tiramisu is a layered dessert of coffee-soaked biscuits and whipped mascarpone cream, dusted with cocoa. It is one of the most famous Italian desserts in the world, and also one of the easiest to make well. It must be made ahead and chilled -- a few hours in the fridge transforms it completely.
sourceNotes: Tiramisu was created in the Veneto region in the 1960s, most likely at the Le Beccherie restaurant in Treviso. It spread across Italy in the 1980s and became one of the defining Italian exports of that decade.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the day before and chill overnight for best results.

content.text: Raw egg yolks are traditional here. If you prefer, whisk them over a bain-marie until thick and pale before folding in the mascarpone.

items.prepNote: use 2 tbsp cocoa powder for dusting
use 4 tbsp marsala or coffee liqueur

content.text: Mix the cooled coffee with the marsala or liqueur in a shallow dish. Set aside.
Whisk the egg yolks with the sugar until pale and thick. This takes about 3-4 minutes with an electric whisk.
Beat the mascarpone until smooth, then fold it into the egg yolk mixture.
In a separate clean bowl, whisk the egg whites to stiff peaks. Fold them gently into the mascarpone mixture in three stages.
Dip each savoiardo briefly in the coffee -- one second per side. Do not soak them.
Arrange a layer of dipped biscuits in a dish. Spread half the mascarpone mixture on top.
Repeat with a second biscuit layer and the rest of the cream. Dust generously with cocoa. Chill for at least 4 hours.

items.symptom: The cream layer is runny and does not set
items.cause: The egg whites were under-whipped, or the biscuits released too much liquid.
items.fix: Whisk the whites to stiff peaks before folding. Dip biscuits for one second only on each side -- they absorb quickly.

items.cause: The savoiardi were left in the coffee too long.
items.fix: A quick one-second dip per side is enough. The biscuits will continue to absorb moisture from the cream as it chills.

items.symptom: The mascarpone has curdled and gone grainy
items.cause: The mascarpone was cold from the fridge and was beaten too hard.
items.fix: Bring mascarpone to room temperature before using. Beat gently until just smooth -- overworking splits it.

content.text: Tiramisu was invented in the Veneto in the 1960s and spread worldwide within a generation. It is served in every trattoria across Italy as the default dessert. The name means 'pick me up', a reference to the coffee and sugar. Few desserts in the world have travelled further or fared better.
